Same Sky uses PPR (pulses per revolution) for the number of high pulses on output A or B in one turn, and CPR (counts per revolution) for the number of quadrature-decoded state changes, which is PPR multiplied by 4. However, some manufacturers use "CPR" to mean cycles per revolution, which equals PPR. Across the industry, the terms PPR, CPR, LPR (lines per revolution on an optical disk) and "resolution" are not used consistently.[2][4] Mixing up the two meanings of CPR makes a robot's computed travel distance wrong by a factor of four. A good habit is to turn a newly mounted wheel exactly one full turn by hand while logging the raw count, to confirm the true multiplier. As a rule of thumb, choose an encoder whose resolution in edges per revolution is somewhat finer than the smallest positioning error you can accept; to know a joint to ±1°, that means more than 360 edges per revolution.[4]
